lines: I’m getting on the bus to the other world, farewell.
When I was a child, I couldn’t count the lives I took.
I buried small lives, smiled calmly, and headed home.
Now that I think about it, I’m glad I’m the first to die.
The stale air around me feels thick.
It steals my sense of worth.
Lifelines are just unnecessarily long.
They’re nothing but useless wrinkles.
Deep inside, my heart laments a trivial view of life.
I spit out the ideals that pierce my ears.
What value could a life that wants to vanish have?
You call me selfish? You don’t even know a fragment of my thoughts.
In a few decades over there, I’ll just be a nuisance.
Then stab me, kill me, take everything, and leave.
I’m getting on the bus to the other world, farewell.
I can’t forget being mocked in my childhood.
Unfathomable absurdity clings to my mind.
Now I wonder why I swallowed it.
Ah, I wish I’d fought back.
I crawl through the hazy crowd.
I’ll show my worth.
Happiness theories are just unnecessarily deep.
They’re merely useless words.
A shallow heart is driven by an unremarkable restlessness.
Only time passes, and I can’t go back.
What kind of seed could sprout in a life that wants to vanish?
You think I’m a hassle? I don’t need your voice.
It’ll just be carried over decades ahead.
Then stab me, kill me, take everything, and leave.
Does a life that wants to vanish have any meaning?
Does such a life have any dream?
It doesn’t.
What value could a life that wants to vanish have?
It’s painful, you say you understand? Don’t act like you get it.
Even decades ahead there, you’ll still be lamenting.
Then stab me, kill me, take everything, and leave.
That’s the first and last desperate struggle I can make.
I’m getting on the bus to the other world, farewell.
But I regret, I scream, and the rain falls.
